name: Dean Spanos

views.text: A proven, famous coach is worth paying when the moment comes.
People say we will not spend; the record will show otherwise.
My son runs football operations; I sign off on the big decisions.
A franchise quarterback demands a coach who can win now.
Los Angeles is a market we have to win over with results.
A losing season is a reason to clean house completely.

signatures: issues a short prepared statement for hires
leaves the press conference to family executives
want: Make the Chargers a contender that wins Los Angeles over (medium).
fear: The frugal label sticking and costing him the best people (medium).
voice: Reserved and rarely heard, speaking through prepared statements. Praise for hires is warm but brief; leaves explanations to his son and the football staff.

evidence.summary: Column on the Chargers' reputation for not spending on coaches, staff and facilities, arguing they should pay what it takes for Jim Harbaugh.
Covers the Harbaugh hire as a bold move by Spanos, who praised Harbaugh in a prepared statement.
John Spanos, president of football operations, led the public response to the Staley and Telesco firings and said the club would do whatever it takes to win.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
